primary_antecedent.receiving_contribution: Antecedent for the common-region bootstrap. This independent proof retains the full matrix lower terms, rough normal source, actual weak Dirichlet domain and finite parametrix errors, and supplies explicit geometry, exercises and an original figure.

source_correspondence: B0 retains the actual H1 solution, an L2 source with all tangential orders on a fixed region, smooth value data, scalar real quadratic principal symbol and arbitrary complex matrix lower terms. The conclusion uses one neighborhood for all orders.

B1 proves continuity of the full broken cap map through strict tangency. A smooth minimum section gives x=mu+t squared times a positive smooth factor; the reflection jump tends to zero at rate square root of minus mu. The accessible region is open, conic and stable under taking the glancing subpath anchor. It is chosen before any Sobolev order.

B2 constructs the globally elliptic full matrix extension with the correct Dirichlet stable-space isomorphism. All normal cutoff derivatives and the full commutator remain. The actual rough solution has restriction order (2,-1) by normal recovery. The exact VB left identity has a finite one-order error gain, not an infinite smoothing gain; finite iteration at fixed normal index gives X(s+1). No unsupported all-normal-regularity hypothesis is imposed on u or f.

B3 proves transverse Dirichlet reflection for the full matrix lower class and rough normal source. The negative branch reaches the regular cap. The exact full-root commuting cutoff, its actual initial value, negative-order weak uniqueness and Duhamel formula give every tangential outgoing order. The scalar RF theorem is not silently applied to a matrix problem.

B4 proves the full-frequency anisotropic mapping of ordinary negative-order operators by a weighted Fourier kernel and both Schur integrals. A matrix high-normal parametrix controls pure normal frequencies from the actual rough source. Compact finite-normal coverage then transfers ordinary propagation into the required tangential mixed norm.

B5 proves the half-step at every point of the same open region. Elliptic and hyperbolic boundary points and glancing events are treated separately; the glancing anchor of every needed path belongs to the induction region. A finite parametrix cover handles any compact tester after the local gains. Neighborhoods and constants can depend on order without shrinking the fixed induction region.

B6 fixes one compressed cone and compares every complete compressed order with tangential orders. The full normal commutator includes the order-minus-one coefficient multiplying the normal derivative. Proper input cutoffs, tangentially separated errors and their full normal commutators act on the original H1 input. This gives the smooth-front closure criterion on one common neighborhood.

B7 returns to the original natural-dual weak Dirichlet problem through the exact BPL representative, NR matrix gauge and LG/ECR elliptic correction. Smooth nonzero trace of the corrected solution is not confused with zero original trace. Full complex conjugation reverses the tangent germ and all lower derivative signs, yielding the strict singular-segment statement for the Dirichlet domain only.

Three complete exercises check the continuous cap displacement with its square-root corner, finite fractional tangential iteration, and a Sobolev counterexample to an order-dependent neighborhood argument. Thirty-nine exact identities or inequalities supplement the analytic proofs.
All 304 formulas and 33 displays parse; all display and figure extents remain accessible on mobile.
The proof map identifies the exact earlier programme prerequisites. Linked human components retain their authorship and licence notices.
